labs.alt: Simulation scene: a growth chamber of Fast Plant seedlings seen from above
labs.title: Artificial Selection
labs.q: Can extreme selection change expression of a quantitative trait in a population in one generation?
labs.sim: Count trichomes on Fast Plants, select parents, and grow the next generation.
labs.description: Explore artificial selection in a free AP Biology virtual lab. Count Fast Plant trichomes, select parents, compare generations, and analyze your results.

labs.alt: Simulation scene: a gene-pool jar of allele beads beside a graph of allele frequency over generations
labs.title: Mathematical Modeling: Hardy-Weinberg
labs.q: How can mathematical models be used to investigate the relationship between allele frequencies in populations of organisms and evolutionary change?
labs.sim: Spreadsheet-style model with selection, mutation, migration and drift.
labs.description: Model Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium in a free AP Biology virtual lab. Investigate allele frequencies, natural selection, mutation, migration, and genetic drift.

labs.alt: Simulation scene: a fossil slab of a small feathered animal
labs.title: Comparing DNA Sequences with BLAST
labs.q: How can bioinformatics be used as a tool to determine evolutionary relationships and to better understand genetic diseases?
labs.sim: Build a cladogram, then align a mystery gene against a sequence database.
labs.description: Investigate evolutionary relationships in a free AP Biology virtual lab. Compare DNA sequences with simulated BLAST, build cladograms, and fit molecular clocks.

labs.alt: Simulation scene: dialysis-tubing bags in cups of solution
labs.title: Diffusion and Osmosis
labs.q: What causes my plants to wilt if I forget to water them?
labs.sim: Agar cubes, dialysis-tube model cells, potato cores, and plasmolysis.
labs.description: Explore diffusion and osmosis in a free AP Biology virtual lab using agar cubes, dialysis bags, potato cores, plasmolysis, and water-potential calculations.

labs.alt: Simulation scene: two cups of leaf disks under a lamp, with disks floating in the bicarbonate cup
labs.title: Photosynthesis
labs.q: What factors affect the rate of photosynthesis in living leaves?
labs.sim: Floating leaf disk assay under changing light, CO₂ and temperature.
labs.description: Investigate photosynthesis with a free AP Biology floating leaf disk virtual lab. Test light, carbon dioxide, and temperature; calculate ET50 and compare rates.

labs.alt: Simulation scene: two microrespirometers in a water bath
labs.title: Cellular Respiration
labs.q: What factors affect the rate of cellular respiration in multicellular organisms?
labs.sim: Microrespirometers with germinating seeds, beads, and temperature.
labs.description: Measure cellular respiration in a free AP Biology virtual lab. Use simulated respirometers and gas sensors to compare seeds, temperature, and respiration rates.

labs.alt: Simulation scene: stained onion root-tip cells under the microscope
labs.title: Cell Division: Mitosis and Meiosis
labs.q: How do eukaryotic cells divide to produce genetically identical cells or to produce gametes with half the normal DNA?
labs.sim: Onion root tip counts, chi-square, meiosis models, and Sordaria crossing over.
labs.description: Explore mitosis and meiosis in a free AP Biology virtual lab. Count onion root-tip cells, model chromosome movement, and investigate Sordaria crossing over.

labs.alt: Simulation scene: a lab bench with a tube rack, an ice bucket and a 42 °C water bath
labs.title: Bacterial Transformation
labs.q: How can we use genetic engineering techniques to manipulate heritable information?
labs.sim: pGLO transformation, heat shock, four plates, and transformation efficiency.
labs.description: Explore pGLO bacterial transformation in a free AP Biology virtual lab. Simulate heat shock, compare growth and fluorescence, and calculate transformation efficiency.

labs.alt: Simulation scene: a stained agarose gel with DNA bands beside a power supply
labs.title: Restriction Enzyme Analysis of DNA
labs.q: How can we use genetic information to identify and profile individuals?
labs.sim: Digest lambda DNA, run a gel, and size fragments from a standard curve.
labs.description: Analyze DNA in a free AP Biology virtual lab. Digest lambda DNA with restriction enzymes, run gel electrophoresis, fit a standard curve, and compare profiles.

labs.alt: Simulation scene: shelves of Fast Plants under a light bank
labs.title: Energy Dynamics
labs.q: What factors govern energy capture, allocation, storage, and transfer between producers and consumers in a terrestrial ecosystem?
labs.sim: Fast Plant biomass and butterfly larvae energy budgets with a live energy-flow diagram.
labs.description: Investigate ecosystem energy dynamics in a free AP Biology virtual lab. Measure Fast Plant biomass and model energy capture and transfer to butterfly larvae.

labs.alt: Simulation scene: a plant cutting in a water-filled potometer
labs.title: Transpiration
labs.q: What factors, including environmental variables, affect the rate of transpiration in plants?
labs.sim: Stomata peels under the microscope and whole-plant water loss.
labs.description: Investigate transpiration in a free AP Biology virtual lab. Count stomata, measure plant water loss, and test how environmental conditions affect transpiration.

labs.alt: Simulation scene: fruit flies climbing in an upright vial
labs.title: Fruit Fly Behavior
labs.q: What environmental factors trigger a fruit fly response?
labs.sim: A two-chamber choice test with live fly movement and chi-square.
labs.description: Explore fruit fly behavior in a free AP Biology virtual lab. Investigate geotaxis and choice chambers, design controlled trials, and analyze chi-square results.

labs.alt: Simulation scene: a rack of pH tubes turning brown as the enzyme works
labs.title: Enzyme Activity
labs.q: How do abiotic or biotic factors influence the rates of enzymatic reactions?
labs.sim: Turnip peroxidase and guaiacol color changes across pH, temperature and concentration.
labs.description: Investigate enzyme activity in a free AP Biology virtual lab. Measure turnip peroxidase reactions and test pH, temperature, enzyme, and substrate concentration.
